paragraphs.text: Lesson 10, ordering drinks, coffee, and pizza.
I hope you're still hungry because today you're going to learn how to order drinks at a bar,
order coffee at a cafe, and order pizza for delivery.
Conversation number one, ordering a drink.
The person who works at the bar serving drinks is called the bartender.
This word can be used for a man or a woman.
Here's a conversation you might have with him.
Hi there.
What can I get for you?
What do you have on tap?
Guinness, Heineken, Corona, and Sam Adams.
Hmm.
On second thought, I'd like something a little stronger.
Do you have any drink specials?
It's happy hour, so all our cocktails are half-price.
Alright, I'll have a strawberry daiquiri.
Coming right up.
Do you want to start a tab?
No, that's okay.
How much do I owe you?
Four dollars and twenty-five cents.
Here's your change.
That's okay.
Conversation vocabulary and phrases.
In informal spoken English, especially in questions, the word you is often pronounced
yah.
That's why the bartender says, what can I get for you?
The question, what do you have on tap is asking about the types of beer that the bar has
available.
Beer that is on tap is served from a barrel and faucet, like in the picture, not in a can
or bottle.
There are four basic types of drinks you can get in a bar.
One is beer.
There are many different types of beer, including light beer, dark beer, imported beer, and non-alcoholic
beer.
The two main types of beer are ale, which has a stronger, more flavorful taste, and lager
with a cleaner, smoother taste.
Here's some phrases you might use for ordering beer.
I'll have a Budweiser.
Can I get a pint of Sam Adams?
Three corona's please.
Another type of drink is wine.
Wine comes in two major colors, red wine and white wine, and each color can come in two different
tastes, sweet wine and dry wine.
Dry wine is not very sweet.
Many bars and restaurants have a house wine, which is the wine they serve most frequently.
Here are some phrases for ordering wine.
I'll have a glass of the house wine.
Can we get a bottle of white wine?
Two glasses of red wine please.
A third type of drink is cocktails and mixed drinks.
These drinks are alcohol mixed with other liquids, like fruit juice or soda.
Here are some phrases for that.
I'll have a ramen coke.
Can I get a margarita?
One screwdriver and one bloody Mary please.
And a fourth type of drink that you can order in a bar is called shots.
Shots are small portions of strong alcohol, drunk pure, without mixing it with juice or
any other ingredients.
For example, I'll have a shot of whiskey.
Can we get a round of tequila shots?
Two shots of vodka please.
You can also order strong alcoholic drinks like whiskey, either on the rocks, which means
with ice, or straight up, which means without ice.
Happy hour is a time usually just after work, like from 5 to 7 pm, when many bars offer drinks
at a reduced price.
When the bartender asks, do you want to start a tab, he wants to know if you will pay later.
A tab means that you will have many drinks and only pay at the end before you leave.
Also, in spoken English, the words want to are often pronounced wana.
In the United States, as in restaurants, you need to leave a tip for the bartender.
At the end of the conversation, the phrase, that's okay means the bartender can keep the
extra money.
If you are drinking with friends, you can tell the bartender, can we get another round?
A round means everyone will have another of the same drink they just finished.
If you want to pay for a drink for your friend, you can say, it's on me, or this one's on me.
If you want to meet someone, especially if you are a man and you want to start a conversation
with a woman, you can say, can I buy you a drink?
Have fun at the bar, but make sure you have a designated driver.
That's a person who isn't drinking any alcohol, who will be sober, not drunk, in order to drive
everyone home.
Now let's learn about ordering coffee.
Here are four ways to ask for coffee.
Can I get?
Could I have?
I'd like and I'll have.
There's not much difference between these four phrases.
You can use any of them.
Now, here are some different ways to have your coffee.
You can have iced coffee, that's cold coffee with ice, black coffee, meaning with no milk,
coffee with milk, or coffee with soy milk.
Soy milk is a non-dairy alternative to milk.
You can order your coffee in different sizes, like small, medium, or large, and you could get
a regular coffee that's with caffeine, or a decaf coffee that's without caffeine.
You can also order your coffee with whipped cream.
There are also many different types of coffee.
Here are some of the most common.
An espresso is a very small, very strong coffee.
A latte is an espresso plus hot milk.
A cappuccino is espresso plus hot milk plus foam.
A macchiato is an espresso plus a little bit of milk.
The word mocha refers to espresso plus hot milk plus chocolate, and a white mocha is made
with white chocolate.
Finally, an americano is an espresso plus water.
We also have different types of milk.
Whole milk is milk with the most fat.
Half and half is a mixture of 50% milk and 50% cream.
2% milk is milk with 2% fat.
1% milk is milk with 1% fat.
And skim milk, or non-fat milk, is milk with 0% fat.
Finally, if you like your coffee to be sweet, you can choose between sugar and sweetener.
Sweetener is artificial sugar with fewer calories.
So, to combine all these elements into a phrase, you might make your order like this.
Can I get a medium black decaf coffee?
Could I have a large iced coffee with soy milk?
I'll have a large mocha with whipped cream.
I'd like a small latte.
Can I get a medium cappuccino?
Etc.
Finally, the server may ask you, for here or to go.
They want to know if you will stay in the cafe to eat and drink.
That's for here.
Or if you will take your food and drink and leave.
That's to go.
Conversation number two, ordering a pizza.
Armando's pizza?
Can I take your order?
I'd like a large pizza for delivery.
Any toppings?
What do you have?
Pepperoni, mushrooms, onions, peppers, sausage, olives, bacon, tomatoes, anchovies, and extra
cheese.
Okay, I'll have mushrooms and peppers, please.
Actually, if you order two toppings, the third one is free.
Oh, alright.
Could you put mushrooms and peppers on one half and extra cheese on the other?
Yep.
Anything to drink?
Two cans of Sprite.
You might as well get a bottle that's actually less expensive than two cans.
Uh, sure, why not?
Okay, your total is 2380.
Could I have your name, address, and phone number?
Laura Jones, 1587 Market Street, Apartment 701, and my phone number is 5551299.
Thanks.
Your order will be delivered in about 30 minutes.
Let's learn the vocabulary and phrases from this conversation.
Pizza is usually common three sizes, small, medium, and large.
The ingredients, like meat and vegetables that you put on top of a pizza, are called toppings.
In most pizza places, the basic pizza is one price and each topping costs extra to add.
You can also ask for half, 50% of the pizza to have one topping, and the other half to have
a different topping.
The expression why not means yes or okay or I have no objections.
With most deliveries you have two payment options.
You can pay by credit card over the phone, or you can pay in cash, which you give to the
person who delivers the pizza.
You should also give a tip of 15% to the person who delivers the pizza.
Why is it necessary to give so many tips in the United States to servers, bartenders, and
delivery people?
Well, most of these jobs pay extremely low salaries, often less than minimum wage, so the
workers depend on receiving these tips to survive and get a decent salary.
You've finished lesson 10 of the everyday English speaking course.
Today's speaking challenge is to call me and leave a message ordering three things.
Order a drink, order coffee, and order a pizza, using the phrases from this lesson.
Tomorrow we're going to switch gears.
That means change topics, and talk about going to the post office and the bank.
